questions.q: Why did Yahweh declare punishment against Moab?
questions.a: Yahweh declared punishment against Moab because they burned the bones of the king of Edom.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do to the city of Kerioth?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would send a fire that would destroy the fortresses of the city of Kerioth.

questions.q: What did Yahweh declare he would do to the judge and other leaders of Moab?
questions.a: Yahweh declared that he would kill the judge and and officials of Moab.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh declare punishment against Judah?
questions.a: Yahweh declared punishment against Judah because Judah rejected the law of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Yahweh declare he would do to the fortresses of Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh declared he would burn down the fortresses of Jerusalem.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel do to the righteous and the needy?
questions.a: The people of Israel sold the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh declare punishment against Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh declared punishment against Israel because Israel was oppressing poor people.

questions.q: What did the people of Israel do in the temple?
questions.a: They drank wine bought with fines in the temple of their God.

questions.q: How had the Israelites been able to defeat the Amorites?
questions.a: The Israelites had been able to defeat the Amorites because Yahweh destroyed the Amorites for them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do for the Israelites after he brought them out of Egypt?
questions.a: Yahweh led the Israelites in the wilderness for forty years and gave them the land of the Amorites as their own.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh choose from among the Israelites?
questions.a: Yahweh chose some of their young men to be prophets and others to be Nazirites.

questions.q: What did the Israelites do with the prophets Yahweh had chosen for them?
questions.a: The Israelites commanded the prophets not to prophesy.

questions.q: What did the Israelites do with the Nazirites Yahweh had chosen from among them?
questions.a: The Israelites forced the Nazirites to break their vows not to drink wine.

questions.q: What did Yahweh declare he would do to Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh declared he would make them unable to escape his punishment.

questions.q: What will the swift person, the strong person, and the mighty person not be able to do?
questions.a: The swift person will not be able to run fast enough to escape, the strong person will not be able to add to his own strength, and the mighty person will not be able to rescue himself.

questions.q: What did Yahweh declare concerning archers, fast runners, and horsemen?
questions.a: Yahweh declared that none of them would be able to save themselves when he comes to punish the nation.

commentary.text: The ingratitude and ruin of Israel.

Verses 1–8 The evil passions of the heart break out in various forms; but the Lord looks to our motives, as well as our conduct. Those that deal cruelly, shall be cruelly dealt with. Other nations were reckoned with for injuries done to men; Judah is reckoned with for dishonour done to God. Judah despised the law of the Lord; and he justly gave them up to strong delusion; nor was it any excuse for their sin, that they were the lies, the idols, after which their fathers walked. The worst abominations and most grievous oppressions have been committed by some of the professed worshippers of the Lord. Such conduct leads many to unbelief and vile idolatry.

We need often to be reminded of the mercies we have received; which add much to the evil of the sins we have committed. They had helps for their souls, which taught them how to make good use of their earthly enjoyments, and were therefore more valuable. Faithful ministers are great blessings to any people; but it is God that raises them up to be so. Sinners' own consciences will witness that he has not been wanting to them in the means of grace. They did what they could to lead believers aside. Satan and his agents are busy to corrupt the minds of young people who look heavenward; they overcome many by drawing them to the love of mirth and pleasure, and into drinking company. Multitudes of young men who bade fair as professors of religion, have erred through strong drink, and have been undone for ever. The Lord complains of sin, especially the sins of his professing people, as a burden to him. And though his long-suffering be tired, his power is not, and so the sinner will find to his cost. When men reject God's word, adding obstinacy to sin, and this becomes the general character of a people, they will be given up to misery, notwithstanding all their boasted power and resources. May we then humble ourselves before the Lord, for all our ingratitude and unfaithfulness.
